title: Ensure nodev option set on /tmp partition
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 1.1.2.1.2: Ensure nodev option set on /tmp partition

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

parameters.name: partition
parameters.description: Filesystem partition to check for mount options

parameters.name: fs_option
parameters.description: Filesystem mount option to check on the target partition (e.g. nodev, nosuid, noexec)

fields.name: raw_mount_details
fields.description: Raw output from findmnt for the target partition

steps.name: Check if a separate partition exists for /tmp
steps.function: 1. Check if a separate partition exists for /tmp using command: `findmnt -kn /tmp`. Expected result: a mount point entry for /tmp is returned (if nothing is returned, the check is SKIPPED as no separate /tmp partition exists).

steps.name: Check that the nodev mount option is set on the /tmp partition
steps.function: 2. Check that the nodev mount option is set on the /tmp partition using command: `findmnt -kn /tmp | grep -v nodev`. Expected result: nothing should be returned (empty output indicates nodev is set).

steps.function: 3. Determine overall compliance status: PASS if the /tmp partition exists and the nodev option is set (grep returns nothing); SKIP if no separate /tmp partition exists (findmnt returns nothing); FAIL if the /tmp partition exists but the nodev option is not set (grep returns output).

steps.function: 4. Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR) derived from the last requirement's status variable.

reference_procedure:
- IF - a separate partition exists for /tmp, verify that the nodev option is set.
Run the following command to verify that the nodev mount option is set.
Example:
# findmnt -kn /tmp | grep -v nodev

Nothing should be returned
